entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 54:1-7 . See on Ps 4:1 , title; Ps 32:1 , title; for the history, see 1Sa 23:19, 29; 26:1-25 . After an earnest cry for help, the Psalmist promises praise in the assurance of a hearing.

entries.heading: 3. strangers
entries.text: 3. strangers --perhaps Ziphites. oppressors --literally, "terrible ones" ( Isa 13:11; 25:3 ). Such were Saul and his army. not set . . . them --acted as atheists, without God's fear (compare Ps 16:8 ).
4. (Compare Ps 30:10 ). with them --on their side, and for me (compare Ps 46:11 ).

entries.heading: 5. He shall . . . evil
entries.text: 5. He shall . . . evil --or, "Evil shall return on" ( Ps 7:16 ) my enemies or watchers, that is, to do me evil ( Ps 6:7 ). in thy truth --Thy verified promise.

entries.heading: 6. I will freely,
entries.text: 6. I will freely, &c.--or, present a freewill offering ( Le 7:16; Nu 15:3 ).

entries.heading: 7. mine eye . . . desire
entries.text: 7. mine eye . . . desire --(compare Ps 59:10; 112:8 ), expresses satisfaction in beholding the overthrow of his enemies as those of God, without implying any selfish or unholy feeling (compare Ps 52:6, 7 ).
